name: Lindy.ai
summary: An AI teammate that lives in Slack: @mention it and it works across your other tools, sits in meetings for shared context and runs jobs on a schedule.
best_for: teams that live in Slack and want one shared teammate that sits in their meetings, runs scheduled routines and drafts replies inside the tools they already use
skip_if: you want flat, predictable automation costs across a large team: Lindy charges for every seat that touches it and the credits expire each cycle, so you pay for people whether or not they used their allowance
honest_knock: Cost tracks headcount as well as output: every colleague who so much as @mentions Lindy in Slack takes a seat, and a seat you remove runs to the end of the cycle with no mid-cycle proration. Credits are sized in ranges (an everyday ask is 2-250, a big build 1,000-2,500), so a month is still an estimate. And the entry price itself was served in two versions on 8 November 2026: $29.99 for 3,000 credits or $49.99 for 5,000.

pricing.plans_source: hand-curated from the vendor's pricing page
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-11-08, read on their own pricing page by plain fetch, ten times) Team starts at $29.99/mo per user for 3,000 credits on some fetches of lindy.ai/pricing and at $49.99/mo per user for 5,000 credits on others: the page serves two versions of the entry level, and 7 of 10 pricing-page fetches on 8 November showed $49.99. The plan line-up changed since 2 October: Plus, Pro and Max are gone. There is now a Free start with $50 in credits for 7 days and no credit card required, one Team plan where you pick a monthly credit level, and quote-only Enterprise. Higher Team levels read the same in both versions: 6,000 credits $59.99, 8,000 $79.99, 15,000 $99.99, 20,000 $149.99, 35,000 $199.99, 45,000 $299.99, and team levels of 70,000 ($399.98), 105,000 ($599.97), 175,000 ($999.95), 350,000 ($1,999.90), 700,000 ($3,999.80) and 1,750,000 credits ($9,999.50). The page says every active user in the workspace is billed, from the entry amount for the entry credits each. Credits pool across the team; monthly credits refresh each billing cycle and do not roll over. Top-ups are now sold at $10 per 1,000 credits, and top-up credits stay until used. Anyone who uses Lindy takes a seat, including colleagues who only @mention it in Slack; those who join through Slack get a 7-day free trial first, direct signups are billed straight away.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 31 October 2026: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We stopped at the start of the trial because it asked for a card.
findings: After sign-up Lindy asks how you heard about it, then offers to connect your work email and calendar. That step can be skipped.
The next screen asks for a card before the trial starts: 'First 7 days free, then $49.99/month. Cancel anytime.' We found no way past it without a card.
The pricing material we read before the test said no credit card was required. On the email sign-up route we used, that did not hold.
We did not enter a card, so we could not test the assistant itself.
